audit_result.proof_trace: The `refund()` function enforces only the upper bound of the refund window via `whenRefundPeriodNotOver` (checks `block.timestamp < refundEndTime`), but has no lower-bound check for `block.timestamp > endTime`. Since `refundEndTime = endTime + refundPeriodSeconds`, refund() succeeds during the active sale period (startTime ≤ block.timestamp < endTime) because that timestamp trivially satisfies `< refundEndTime`. The proof fails: the invariant `endTime < block.timestamp ≤ refundEndTime` is only half-enforced.
audit_result.attack_scenario: An investor calls `invest()` during the active sale, then immediately calls `refund()` before `endTime` — both calls succeed, allowing the investor to exit a committed position mid-sale and undermining capital commitment and price discovery for the raise.

PROP-01b-partial-pre-003.text: refund() only succeeds during refund window (endTime, refundEndTime].
